record.original_question: Construct maximal signed graphs whose smallest adjacency eigenvalue is at least -3.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.16. Construct maximal signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least −3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma = (G, \sigma)$ consisting of a simple graph $G = (V, E)$ together with a sign function $\sigma: E \to \{+1, -1\}$. Its adjacency matrix $A(\Sigma)$ is the symmetric $|V| \times |V|$ matrix whose $(u,v)$-entry equals $\sigma(uv)$ if $uv \in E$ and $0$ otherwise; the eigenvalues of $\Sigma$ are the eigenvalues of $A(\Sigma)$, and the smallest eigenvalue is denoted $\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma)$. Two signed graphs are switching equivalent if one is obtained from the other by selecting a vertex subset $U \subseteq V$ and negating the signs of all edges with exactly one endpoint in $U$; switching equivalence preserves the spectrum.

Call a signed graph $\Sigma$ on vertex set $V$ maximal with smallest eigenvalue at least $-3$ if $\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma) \ge -3$ and no signed graph $\Sigma'$ on the same vertex set $V$ that strictly contains $\Sigma$ as a signed subgraph (i.e., $E(\Sigma) \subsetneq E(\Sigma')$ and the signs of $\Sigma$ are inherited) satisfies $\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma') \ge -3$.

Problem: Construct, up to switching equivalence and isomorphism, all maximal signed graphs whose smallest adjacency eigenvalue is at least $-3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on signed graphs with bounded smallest eigenvalue (e.g., a structure theory for signed graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue, and results showing 2-integrability under large minimum degree) provide partial structural information but do not give a complete construction of maximal signed graphs with $\lambda_{\min} \ge -3$. The classification problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A structure theory for signed graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue
status_evidence.snippet: Develops structural results for signed graphs with a fixed smallest eigenvalue, generalizing classical Hoffman-type theorems.
status_evidence.claim: Provides structural theory but does not produce a complete classification of maximal signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3.

status_evidence.title: On graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 and their lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Connected graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 and sufficiently large minimum degree are 2-integrable.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for unsigned graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3, but the maximal signed-graph classification is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Edge-signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue greater than -2
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies edge-signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue greater than -2.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous problem at threshold -2 has been resolved, but the threshold -3 case for maximal signed graphs is not.
